generator.params.spur_light.note: A choice of the model's (leaf life, generator revision 44): a short shoot leafs out in at least 0.14 of the open sky's light (fagaceae's 0.1). Once a leaf stayed one season, not two, more light reached the inner crown and more short shoots lived, so the open crown at 80 years held more leaf per crown area than the Urban Tree Database's open-grown white oaks (5.38 against 1.9 to 5.3 m²/m²); at 0.14 it holds about 5.1 and keeps its reference height and dbh.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Quercus garryana: grows 15 m to 20 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Quercus garryana: leaves 10 cm to 15 cm long.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Quercus garryana (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.65 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 5 records in 4 sources); trunks 0.65, branches 0.65. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Gucker 2007, read): trees less than 20 years old did not produce acorns, but production increased with age until trees were nearly 80 years old (epicormic branches bore acorns 5 years after sprouting). It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 20 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a slow, long-lived oak with a broad, rounded crown of crooked, gnarled limbs and deeply lobed, leathery leaves. Not fitted to measurements. Its pipe_tip, pipe_organ and pipe_rings are scaled together (crown calibration, broadleaf revision 9) so that, with the leaf its crown now keeps, its trunk reaches the reference dbh of 50 cm at 80 years again.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 15 m tall and 50 cm across at breast height at 80 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark, glossy green leaves; pale grey, furrowed bark carrying moss and lichen. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: green acorns about 2.5 cm long in shallow, scaly cups, singly or in pairs. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) is authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: catkins in April and May; acorns green in summer, ripe and falling in September and October. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): light grey bark, furrowed and checkered into scaly ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves of the outer crown small, narrow and deeply lobed, shade leaves inside it larger, broader and shallower, as in other oaks; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured. Leaf (plant roadmap P4): the sprig's lobes rounded (`round` 0.8), as Oregon white oak's are, and `leaf_area` set to the 0.303 m² it then draws on a leaf 1 m long.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
